subject: POC runbook & access checklist — next steps and creds
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@velox.ai>, James Park <james.park@velox.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: POc recap + what we need to kick off

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment overall. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can start the 3-week POC next week:  

Summary / success criteria (as discussed)
- Ingest & inference: Velox should be able to run 1k queries/day against the sample dataset with median latency < 300ms for 256-token requests.
- Output quality: precision@3 >= 0.78 on the representative prompt set we reviewed.
- Stability: no more than 1% error rate over 24h test windows.

POC plan (high level)
- Week 0 (this week): access + config — API key, IP allowlist, SSO invites, provide test dataset and prompt deck.
- Week 1: baseline runs (default model) + quick evaluation metrics.
- Week 2: optimization (batching, cache, quant profile) and re-run.
- Week 3: final report + handoff/next steps.

Owners / asks
- Velox: confirm the two test accounts to invite to SSO (email addresses below) and provide public IP ranges that should be allowed.
- Redwood: provision a scoped API key (read/write inference only), add the IP allowlist, and send SSO invites to Velox test accounts. Marissa will own day-to-day support and Connor will own engineering changes for any model variant we serve.

Attachments: poc-runbook-v1.pdf (detailed runbook), ip-allowlist-template.csv (CSV for your network team)

Next steps (action items)
1) Sarah/Jamess: share confirmation on SSO emails and IP ranges by EOD Friday (2026-03-19).
2) Marissa: create the scoped API key and send the credentials to Sarah once IPs are confirmed.
3) Connor: stand by for any custom model config; we may need to enable a lower-latency kernel.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 15 if needed.

– Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@velox.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Park <james.park@velox.ai>
Date: 2026-03-19T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POc recap + what we need to kick off

Appreciate the clear plan, Dylan — we want to proceed. A few clarifications from our security team:  

- SSO: we'll use Okta. Please send SSO invites to test accounts: test-internal@velox.ai and test-external@velox.ai.
- IP allowlist: our dev cluster egress IPs are 34.120.12.45 and 34.120.12.46 (we'll confirm with infra but these are the primary).
- API key scope: must be limited to inference endpoints and disabled for account-level config.
- Sample data: I uploaded a 2GB sample dataset to our S3 share and added the link in the drive folder you shared. Expect some edge-case prompts in the dataset.

Question: can the API key be time-limited (30 days) and rotated automatically after 14 days? If not, we'll need a secure distribution plan. Also can you confirm whether logs for our test run will be retained for 30 days for debugging?

We'll confirm the IP addresses by EOD. Once we have the SSO invites and key, we'll kick off the baseline run.

Thanks,
Sarah
Product Manager, Velox Analytics

Date: 2026-03-21T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POc runbook & access checklist — provisioning complete

Hi Sarah — quick update, provisioning complete on our side:  

What we did:
- API key: created scoped key id rk_live_scoped_0x9f3. Key set to auto-expire in 30 days per request. Token sent via one-time encrypted link (DocuShare) to both test-internal@velox.ai and test-external@velox.ai.
- IP allowlist: added 34.120.12.45 and 34.120.12.46 to Velox test rule set. Confirmed via simulated handshake from our egress tester.
- SSO invites: Okta invites sent to test-internal@velox.ai and test-external@velox.ai. Accept link expires in 7 days.
- Logs retention: enabled 30-day retention for request logs for the trial project; we will share read-only entries for debugging.

Attachments included: poc-runbook-v1.pdf (updated with provisioning notes), ip-allowlist-template.csv (filled).

Next steps / recommended first run
1) Velox to run baseline suite (prompt-deck v1) and send us metrics export (median lat, p99, error rates) by EOD next Wednesday (2026-03-25).
2) If latency > 300ms median, Connor will schedule a 30-minute tuning window to enable the low-latency kernel and tweak batch size.
3) For any data privacy concerns, James, please share the specific dataset items to isolate; we can create a private project for those tests.

If anything blocks sign-in or key retrieval, reply here and I'll escalate immediately. Looking forward to the run results.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
